scope: Nonlinear dynamics, recurrence analysis, local divergence/Lyapunov estimation, surrogate testing, and empirical return-map context for eyetrajectoriespy.
interpretation_rule: Verification means that the bibliographic record was recovered from a primary publisher, PubMed/PMC, or another authoritative scholarly index. Failure to verify a candidate citation is not evidence that no related work exists and must never be used as proof of novelty.

evidence_tiers.direct_behavioral_gaze: Peer-reviewed application or methods paper using recurrence/RQA on behavioral eye-movement or fixation-sequence data.
evidence_tiers.direct_eye_or_pupil_signal: Peer-reviewed application/methods paper using the method on eye-movement or pupil time-series signals, but not necessarily continuous behavioral scanpath analysis.
evidence_tiers.general_methodology: Foundational or methodological source supporting the algorithm, estimator, null model, or recurrence framework outside a specific behavioral-gaze application.

verified.citation: Anderson, N. C., Bischof, W. F., Laidlaw, K. E. W., Risko, E. F., & Kingstone, A. (2013). Recurrence quantification analysis of eye movements. Behavior Research Methods, 45(3), 842-856.
verified.supports: Direct behavioral eye-movement precedent for RQA applied to fixation sequences and temporal scanpath structure.
verified.does_not_support: Does not by itself validate every continuous-state, windowed, cross-recurrence, or functional-RQA design choice in eyetrajectoriespy.

verified.citation: Gurtner, L. M., Bischof, W. F., & Mast, F. W. (2019). Recurrence quantification analysis of eye movements during mental imagery. Journal of Vision, 19(1), 17.
verified.supports: Direct behavioral-gaze precedent for RQA as a temporal eye-movement analysis alongside spatial scanpath methods.
verified.does_not_support: Does not establish independence of overlapping windowed RQA values or an FDA inferential theorem for RQA-derived functions.

verified.citation: Korda, A. I., Asvestas, P. A., Matsopoulos, G. K., Ventouras, E. M., & Smyrnis, N. (2018). Automatic identification of eye movements using the largest Lyapunov exponent. Biomedical Signal Processing and Control, 41, 10-20.
verified.supports: Direct eye-movement signal-analysis precedent for largest-Lyapunov/log-divergence methods in saccade and blink identification.
verified.does_not_support: Does not establish that a positive behavioral-scanpath LLE proves deterministic chaos, nor that LLE is a novel eye-movement method.

verified.citation: Mesin, L., Monaco, A., & Cattaneo, R. (2013). Investigation of nonlinear pupil dynamics by recurrence quantification analysis. BioMed Research International, 2013, 420509.
verified.supports: Direct pupil-signal precedent for nonlinear recurrence quantification.
verified.does_not_support: Does not establish a behavioral scanpath interpretation for pupil recurrence metrics.

verified.citation: Piu, P., Serchi, V., Rosini, F., & Rufa, A. (2019). A cross-recurrence analysis of the pupil size fluctuations in steady scotopic conditions. Frontiers in Neuroscience, 13, 407.
verified.supports: Direct pupil-signal precedent for cross-recurrence analysis.
verified.does_not_support: Does not imply that cross-recurrence automatically time-aligns two trajectories or establishes causal synchronization.

verified.citation: Fink, L., Simola, J., Tavano, A., Lange, E., Wallot, S., & Laeng, B. (2024). From pre-processing to advanced dynamic modeling of pupil data. Behavior Research Methods, 56, 1376-1412.
verified.supports: Modern methodological precedent discussing RQA and signal-to-signal dynamic analysis for pupil time series, including assumptions and software context.
verified.does_not_support: Does not make every recurrence analysis design appropriate for gaze coordinates or remove the need for method-specific sampling contracts.

verified.citation: Eckmann, J.-P., Oliffson Kamphorst, S., & Ruelle, D. (1987). Recurrence plots of dynamical systems. Europhysics Letters, 4(9), 973-977.
verified.does_not_support: Does not provide eye-tracking-specific interpretation or parameter-selection rules.

verified.citation: Marwan, N., Romano, M. C., Thiel, M., & Kurths, J. (2007). Recurrence plots for the analysis of complex systems. Physics Reports, 438(5-6), 237-329.
verified.supports: General definitions, variants, interpretation, and cautions for recurrence plots and RQA.
verified.does_not_support: Does not establish behavioral-eye-tracking novelty or an automatic parameter policy.

verified.citation: Coco, M. I., & Dale, R. (2014). Cross-recurrence quantification analysis of categorical and continuous time series: an R package. Frontiers in Psychology, 5, 510.
verified.supports: General CRQA methodology for continuous and categorical behavioral time series, including lag/coupling interpretation.
verified.does_not_support: Does not mean cross-recurrence performs synchronization or time alignment automatically.

verified.citation: Wallot, S., & Leonardi, G. (2018). Analyzing multivariate dynamics using cross-recurrence quantification analysis (CRQA), diagonal-cross-recurrence profiles (DCRP), and multidimensional recurrence quantification analysis (MdRQA) - a tutorial in R. Frontiers in Psychology, 9, 2232.
verified.supports: Practical CRQA and multidimensional recurrence methodology in cognitive/behavioral time-series analysis.
verified.does_not_support: Does not establish that CRQA alone identifies causal coupling.

verified.citation: Fraser, A. M., & Swinney, H. L. (1986). Independent coordinates for strange attractors from mutual information. Physical Review A, 33(2), 1134-1140.
verified.does_not_support: Does not justify silent automatic delay selection for finite noisy gaze data.

verified.citation: Kennel, M. B., Brown, R., & Abarbanel, H. D. I. (1992). Determining embedding dimension for phase-space reconstruction using a geometrical construction. Physical Review A, 45(6), 3403-3411.
verified.does_not_support: Does not provide a universal eye-tracking embedding-dimension cutoff.

verified.citation: Rosenstein, M. T., Collins, J. J., & De Luca, C. J. (1993). A practical method for calculating largest Lyapunov exponents from small data sets. Physica D, 65(1-2), 117-134.
verified.supports: Estimator family implemented by eyetrajectoriespy for nearest-neighbor mean log-divergence and fitted slope.
verified.does_not_support: Does not create a universal minimum sample-size threshold or prove chaos from a positive fitted slope.

verified.citation: Kantz, H. (1994). A robust method to estimate the maximal Lyapunov exponent of a time series. Physics Letters A, 185(1), 77-87.
verified.supports: Independent methodological precedent for local-divergence-based maximal Lyapunov estimation and sensitivity thinking.
verified.does_not_support: Is not the estimator currently exposed by eyetrajectoriespy and should not be cited as if Kantz's algorithm were implemented.

verified.citation: Schreiber, T., & Schmitz, A. (1996). Improved surrogate data for nonlinearity tests. Physical Review Letters, 77(4), 635-638.
verified.supports: IAAFT-style iterative surrogate construction and null-model framing.
verified.does_not_support: Does not make rejection proof of deterministic chaos or a unique nonlinear mechanism.

verified.citation: Schreiber, T., & Schmitz, A. (2000). Surrogate time series. Physica D, 142(3-4), 346-382.
verified.supports: Surrogate-data hypothesis-testing framework, practical caveats, and the requirement to state the null model.
verified.does_not_support: Does not validate independent univariate IAAFT as a multivariate x-y gaze surrogate preserving cross-structure.
